# Issue #982: Defect triage 2026-10-29: fix in moved Nikaia, defer the rest to its move

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/982).

`note` · opened 2026-10-29 · updated 2026-10-29 · 0 comments

Owner's direction (2026-10-29): a compiler defect is fixed now when its code has already moved to Nikaia completely (`crates/nikaia-std/src/tools/*.nika`, lowered). A defect whose fix lands in Rust that is still to move waits for that move, so the work is not done twice. Self-hosting goes on.

The probes were re-run with `target/fast/nikaia` at de0bb82 (0.0.1296), each fix site was found by grepping `tools/*.nika` against `crates/nikaia/src`, and the issues were sorted.

## Counts

| Class | Meaning | Count | Issues |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | :--- |
| A | the fix lands in moved Nikaia: fix now | 35 | the lanes below |
| B | the fix lands in Rust still to move: waits | 5 | #935, #939, #587, #972, #690 |
| C | fixed already, or a duplicate: closed by hand | 6 | #713, #914, #916, #946, #976, #977 |
| D | a decision, not a defect: relabelled `decision` | 1 | #625 |

## A: three lanes, separate by file

The order inside each lane puts self-hosting blockers first (`docs/priorities.md`): a workaround in `tools/*.nika` or in the converter that the fix lets us undo, then a false refusal a move meets, then a rustc error reaching users, then message text.

**Lane T: text tiers and keeps** (`text_tiers.nika`, `keeps.nika`, `view_changes.nika`)
1. #958: tuple with a literal into `Vec[(i64, String)]` (the `bounds_walk.nika` ~2293 workaround, NK1106)
2. #980: a nested list's element is not linked to the `mut` parameter (`source_of`/`place_of` lack `Expr::Index`)
3. #967: a list element's text field changed in place (`v[0].name += "!"`)
4. #981: a change in place through a `m[k] ?? jump` view
5. #882: the remaining `String?` half (`classify` keeps a `String?` read through `??`/`match`)
6. #971: NK2305 help names `self`, not the list

**Lane E: lowering** (`emit_*.nika`)
1. #908: `split_once(..) ?? ("", owned)` (three converter workarounds)
2. #915: a pushed `mut String` read through `.trim()` becomes a view (converter workaround `rs2nika_text`)
3. #907: `[..].contains(view)` over literals (converter writes around it)

# Issue #983: async: one concept, task; async is an expression prefix (ADR-async-1..4)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/983).

`ready` · opened 2026-10-30 · updated 2026-10-30 · 4 comments

**Decided (owner, 2026-10-30, third and fourth design rounds; the design round is closed).** Records: [ADR-async-1](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-1.md) (Accepted; its forms changed, see the notes under each D), [ADR-async-2](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-2.md) (Accepted, option D; D9), [ADR-async-3](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-3.md) (Accepted, option C; D7), [ADR-async-4](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-4.md) (Accepted, the surface; D13, D14); ADR-346 D3, D4 changed. Specification: Part I 8.1-8.3, Part II 11-12, Part III (the version raise is the supervisor's).

## The decision in short

* **One concept, task.** Every task is started in a group and lives at most as long as it; it borrows what outlives the group and takes what does not; it has a block and ends with a value, a failure, a crash or `task::OverBudget`, which goes to the group's receiver. Forms state only their group's policy: `async`, `par_iter`, `select`, `supervisor::run`, `serve`, `async(detached)` (async-3).
* **`async` is an expression prefix; no `async let`.** `let x = async e`, `f(async g(), async h())`, `async a() + async b()`: waited where the value is first needed; no handle, no cancel; nothing beside it is `NK2110` (async-4 D1-D3).
* **Handles:** `async(handle) fn { … }` (group-bound `task::ChildHandle`, `join`/`join(within:)`/`cancel`, `NK2122` if it leaves the group), `async(deferred)` (runs from `h.start()`, `NK2121`), `async(detached)` (free `TaskHandle`, = `spawn`) (async-4 D4-D6).
* **Cancel only through `h.cancel()`**; `task::cancel`, `NK2113`, `NK2114` removed (async-4 D10).
* **`within:` on `async(…)` is a deadline counted from the start**, on every form, value or handle: when it runs out the task is cancelled and `task::TimedOut` arrives where the value is first needed or at the `join` (async-3 D7).
* **`h.join(within: d)` is a limit on this wait** (`task::OnTimeout { Keep, Cancel }`, `Keep` by default): by default it throws `task::TimedOut`, the task keeps running and the handle stays live (join again, cancel, detach); `h.join(within: d, on_timeout: task::OnTimeout::Cancel)` cancels the task and uses the handle up. `NK2109`: without `on_timeout: task::OnTimeout::Cancel` the handle is taken only on the success path, and in the `task::TimedOut` handler it must be taken on every path (async-4 D14; changes ADR-346 D3, D4).
* **Failure order for every form:** the task's own `catch`; a `catch` where it arrives (mention, `join`); the fallback after the `async` expression; the receiver. Only a cancellation the program asks for (`h.cancel()`, a losing `select` arm) runs no fallback; a deadline's `task::TimedOut` is a failure and runs it (async-4 D11, D15).
* **Fan-out is `par_iter`**, whose `map`/`filter`/`for_each` lambdas may pause: the compiler runs pieces or one task per element; one rule set (input order, every failure kept, `NK2104`, `NK2107`); `limit:` replaces `workers:`; `NK2119` warns; costs only where needed. **The lambdas of `fold`, `par_pieces`, `par_fold` never pause** (`NK2209`; its help on a `fold` names `map` (pausing) then `fold`, async-2 D9). **The `async` loop is removed**; `async` inside a loop body is `NK2120` (async-2).
* **The names are final** (async-4 D13): `async`, `sync`, `handle`, `deferred`, `detached`, `on_timeout`, `ChildHandle`, `start()`. `spawn` stays reserved until #991. Part I 8.1 is "Pausing Without Marking Functions", Part II 11.1 "Implicit Pausing and the Scheduler"; 12.4 "Racing Tasks" stays (an arm is a task).
* Codes: retired `NK2113`, `NK2114`, `NK2116`, `NK2117`; new `NK2119`-`NK2122`; `NK2109` widened for `join(within:)`.

## Still open

Nothing of the design. Outside it: a pending value or a handle as a `select` arm (ADR-async-1 §6); cancelling siblings at the first failure (ADR-292 §6).

## To build (sub-issues, in order)

1. #984 parser and reserved word (ready)
2. #987 std and runtime, `join(within:)` / `on_timeout` included (ready; memory half waits on #490)
3. #986 checker, `NK2109` for `join(within:)` and the `NK2209` help included (needs #984)
4. #988 lowering, `--overlaps`, the two measurements (needs #986, #987)
5. #989 failure order and sites (needs #988)
6. #990 migration, `spawn` → `async(detached)` included (needs #988, #989)
7. #991 removal of `overlap`, `task::scope`, `spawn` (needs #990)
8. #992 guide and docs (needs #986)

#985 (the `SharedMut` bug) is independent.

Found on the way: `develop`'s default `dev` profile does not build `nikaia` (winnow recursion limit since 4853408); `--profile fast` and `--release` do.

## Comments

### keywan-ghadami, [2026-10-30](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/983#issuecomment-6521307798)

**Back to `decision` (owner, 2026-10-30): the concurrency concepts are not yet round.** #984 and #987 are set to `blocked` on this issue so nobody builds a shape that may change. #985 (the `SharedMut` bug) stays `ready`; it does not depend on this.

The main session reviewed the concurrency vocabulary as it stands on `develop` at 0.0.1303. The owner finds `async` beside `spawn` confusing, and wants to see whether the concepts can be unified first, before any naming: *fewer forms are more*, and differences in meaning should be inferred by the compiler or hang on options.

#### The concepts as specified now

| Concept | Written | Lifetime | Captures | Waited at |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| pausing (implicit) | nothing | - | - | - |
| `sync` | `fn f() sync` | a function property: never pauses | - | - |
| async child with a value | `async let x = e` / `= fn { … }` | its group | borrows | first mention |
| async group with a value | `async let xs = for … { … }` | its group | borrows | first mention |
| async child, no value | `async e`, `async fn { … }`, `async for …` | its group | borrows | group end |
| async group | `async { … }` | its block | - | `}` |
| task | `spawn fn { … }` → `TaskHandle` | may outlive the scope | moves | `h.join()`, or detached |
| race | `select { p = e => … }` | the block | borrows | block, first wins |
| data parallelism | `xs.par_iter().map/fold …` | the call | borrows, may not pause | the call |
| channel | `channel::bounded(n)` | a value | - | `recv` |
| supervisor | `supervisor::run([child(…)])` | until it gives up | duplicates | - |
| connection tasks | `net::serve` | per connection | - | - |

Plus `task::cancel(x)`, `h.cancel()`, `task::Crashed`, `task::OverBudget`, `task::TimedOut`, `task::Admission` and `task::cores()`.

#### Where it is not consistent

1. **`sync` and `async` look like a pair and are not one.** `sync` is a function property (never pauses); `async` means *run beside*. A reader from JS, Rust or C# reads them as "colored / not colored". Part I 8.1 is still titled "Async by Default" in the old sense ("pauses"). *The owner puts naming last.*
2. **"Task" is used unevenly.** The spec says "A child is not a task", yet a child's tools live in `task::` and for memory it is treated as a task. Part II 12.4 is titled "Racing *Tasks*" though a `select` arm is no task. Part I 8.1 says "a task exists only where the program writes one (`spawn`, `par_iter`)" and "a pause never forks one", which `async` now contradicts. A possible reading, as in Swift: everything is a task, either a *child task* (bound to its scope, borrows) or a *free task* (moves, may outlive).
3. **Two spellings for one cancel.** `h.cancel()` and `task::cancel(x)` use the same mechanism.

#### Real overlap in function

4. **`async let xs = for …` and `par_iter`.** Both are parallel loops that yield a list. With a body that never pauses, the child already runs on the pool. `par_iter` cuts into pieces and has `fold`/`merge` and `order:`; `async for` makes one child, with its own memory block, per element, which is expensive for a million pixels. The boundary is clear but drawn nowhere.
5. **`spawn` + `join` in the same scope versus `async let`.** They are nearly the same. `spawn` must move, and its handle can be returned or stored, so it is not redundant, but within one scope `async` would be the better form.

#### What is consistent

`async fn { … }` and `spawn fn { … }` share one shape. `within:` means the same on `join` and `async`. `select`, channels, supervisor and `serve` each have their own job. The boundary errors (`Crashed`, `OverBudget`, `TimedOut`, "only a bug cancels siblings") are uniform.

#### Leftovers in the specification

* Part I line 211 still names `scope.spawn fn { … }` (Part II 12.5): a remnant of `task::scope`, and the wrong section.
* The titles and sentences in points 1-2.

#### The owner's direction for the next round

* First, independent of names: can `par_iter` and `async for` (and further, `async` children and `spawn` tasks) become **one mechanism**, with the differences (pieces or one child each, borrows or moves, bound or detached, pausing or computing) inferred by the compiler or set by options?
* Names (`sync`/`async`, `spawn`) come after that.

# Issue #984: async (ADR-async-4): parser and reserved word

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/984).

`ready` · opened 2026-10-30 · updated 2026-10-30 · 0 comments

Part of #983. Records: [ADR-async-4](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-4.md) D1, D4-D9, D12; [ADR-async-2](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-2.md) D7, D8; [ADR-async-3](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-3.md) D5. Spec: Part I 8.1.2, 8.2, 5.3, the reserved words; Part III `NK2115`, `NK2120`.

The grammar of the new surface, with `overlap` and `spawn` still accepted until the removal issue (#991).

## To build
1. **Reserved words**: `parser::RESERVED_WORDS` (`crates/nikaia-std/src/tools/parse_errors.nika`, lowered) becomes exactly Part I's list: add `async`, drop `overlap` (keep parsing it as a construct until #991). `spawn` stays reserved. This turns `from_is_a_name::the_page_and_the_table_list_the_same_words` green.
2. Parse `async` as a **prefix of an expression** with optional options `(name: expr, … , handle | deferred | detached …)` written in one list without a positional zone: on the right of `=`, as an argument, as an operand, in a tuple, as an expression statement, before `{ … }` (the group) and before `fn { … }` (a lambda run as the task). An optional `catch { … }` directly after the `async` expression is its fallback. The AST names value form, handle form (with its flags), statement form, group, and keeps the options.
3. Refusals: `async` before a function's declaration, a `let` or a loop (`NK2115`); `async` inside a loop body (`NK2120`, help `xs.par_iter().for_each fn(x) { … }`; may also live in the checker, #986).

5. `fmt` formats every form.

# Issue #986: async (ADR-async-4, async-2): checker - wait points, groups, touch sets, handles, par_iter lambdas

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/986).

`blocked` · opened 2026-10-30 · updated 2026-10-30 · 0 comments

Part of #983. Records: [ADR-async-4](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-4.md) D2-D5, D7, D10-D14; [ADR-async-2](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-2.md) D1, D3, D5, D8, D9; [ADR-async-3](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-3.md) D2, D7; ADR-async-1 D5, D7-D9, D11; ADR-346 D3 (changed by async-4 D14). Spec: Part I 8.1.2, 8.2; Part II 12.6; Part III `NK2104`, `NK2107`, `NK2109`, `NK2110`-`NK2112`, `NK2115`, `NK2118`-`NK2122`, `NK1132`, `NK2202`, `NK2203`, `NK2209`. Needs #984 (parser).

## To build
1. **Wait points**: `let x = async e` before the first statement naming any of its names anywhere nested (except a mention inside another task: that task waits); an argument before its call; an operand before its operation; an unnamed binding or statement form at its group's end.
2. **Groups**: the innermost `async { }` in the same function, else the innermost block. `NK2110` for a task with nothing beside it (an argument with no sibling computed beside it, a binding named in the next statement, a statement ending its group; help removes the word); `NK2111` for an `async { }` with no task; `NK2120` for `async` in a loop body.
3. **Captures** (async-3 D2): a child task borrows names bound outside its group and takes those bound in a block that ends earlier (`NK2105`); `async(detached)` takes everything (`NK2101`, the existing `spawn` rules).
4. **Touch sets** (`check_walks.nika`, `touch.nika`): `NK2104` between a bound task and each window statement, between the tasks of one call's arguments / one operation's operands and what is computed beside them, and **a `par_iter` lambda of `map`/`filter`/`for_each` against itself** (the stdout case: `xs.par_iter().for_each fn(x) { println(…) }` is refused); `limit: 1` exempts; C.4. `NK2107` as before.
5. **Pausing `par_iter` lambdas**: `NK2209` no longer asked of `map`/`filter`/`for_each` lambdas; still asked, finally, of `fold`, `par_pieces`, `par_fold` (async-2 D9). **The help of `NK2209` on a `fold` lambda names the chain `map` (pausing) followed by `fold`**, e.g. `xs.par_iter().map fn(u) { http::get(u) }.fold(…)`. Record per site pieces / one task per element in the ledger; `NK2119` (warning) where the committed ledger had pieces and the lambda can now pause, naming the call (the `NK2211` mechanism).
6. **Handles**: `async(handle)` is a `task::ChildHandle[T]`; one that leaves its group is `NK2122`; an unjoined one is waited at the group's end (not `NK2109`). `async(deferred)` not started or cancelled on some path, or started twice: `NK2121` (the path rule `NK2109` uses). `async(detached)` handles keep `NK2109`.
7. **`join(within:)` and `NK2109`** (async-4 D14, Part I 8.2): a `join(within: d)` without `on_timeout: task::OnTimeout::Cancel` takes a `TaskHandle` only on its success path (and on a failure of the task's body). On the path where it throws `task::TimedOut` the handle is still live and must be taken on every path out of the handler: in a `match error` arm for `task::TimedOut`, in an `else` or binding arm that can match it, in the whole handler where it does not match on the error; otherwise `NK2109`. `join(within: d, on_timeout: task::OnTimeout::Cancel)` takes it on both paths. A live `ChildHandle` after a timed-out join is waited at its group's end, not `NK2109`.
8. **Chaining ownership**: read/read allowed; window change refused (`NK2104`); a task moving a pending binding hands it over at its start (`NK2105` later); diamonds.
9. **Types**: `async e` has `e`'s type; the callee sees `T`. `async fn { … }` the lambda's result type. Handles their types.
10. **Jumps**: leaving a task is `NK1132`; `return` inside `async fn { … }` ends the task.
11. **Options**: `limit:` on a one-task form `NK2112`; types of `limit`, `within`, `admission`; `on_timeout: task::OnTimeout` on `join` (`Keep` by default, or `Cancel`); `limit:`/`within:`/`admission:` on `par_iter`, `limit:` on `fold`/`par_fold` (`workers:` refused as an unknown option).
12. **Pausing and locks**: a body holding an `async` form is not `sync` (`NK2202`); an `async` form in an open door `NK2203`.
13. **`NK2118`**: a mention after a `catch` where the failure arrived took it, without a fallback.
14. Tests (`tests/compiler/tests/async_*.nika` with `.stderr`), among them: two tasks printing refused; a `par_iter` lambda printing refused; `limit: 1` accepted; `f(async g())` alone refused; `async` in a loop refused; a child handle returned refused; a deferred handle never started refused; chained read/read accepted; `NK2119` after a ledger change; a `join(within:)` whose `task::TimedOut` handler drops the handle refused (`NK2109`), the same with `on_timeout: task::OnTimeout::Cancel` accepted; a pausing `fold` step refused with the `map`-then-`fold` help.

# Issue #987: async (ADR-async-4, async-2): std and runtime - group runtime, handles, par_iter tasks, admission, task::OverBudget

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/987).

`ready` · opened 2026-10-30 · updated 2026-10-30 · 0 comments

Part of #983. Records: [ADR-async-4](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-4.md) D4-D6, D10, D14; [ADR-async-2](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-2.md) D2-D4, D6; [ADR-async-3](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-3.md) D3, D7; ADR-async-1 D14, D15; ADR-327 D6 (changed); ADR-346 D4 (changed by async-4 D14). Spec: Part I 8.2; Part II Chapter 12 (memory budget, `task::OverBudget`, admission), 12.6; Part III 13.3b, 17.1 `std::task`, the C error code `1102`.

**Dependency:** the memory half of admission and `task::OverBudget` needs ADR-327 D4-D7 built (#490). Until then admission counts descriptors only; steps 1-4 and 6 do not wait.

## To build
1. **The group runtime** in `crates/nikaia-std/src/task.rs` (replacing the `overlap<n>` vehicles and `task::scope`): start, hold an outcome, join in written order, cancel, a `limit` gate; a group of fixed size laid out without an allocation (async-2 D8).
2. **`task::ChildHandle[T]`**: points at the group's slot, no `Send`, no heap; `join()`, `join(within:)`, `cancel()`, `start()` for a deferred one. **`TaskHandle[T]`** gains `start()` for `async(detached, deferred)`; `spawn` stays until #991.
3. **`join(within: d)` is a limit on this wait** (async-4 D14, changes ADR-346 D4, which today's `TaskHandle::join(within:)` builds): when `d` runs out, `join` throws `task::TimedOut`, **the task keeps running and the handle stays live** (joinable again, cancellable, detachable for a `TaskHandle`). `join(within: d, on_timeout: task::OnTimeout::Cancel)` cancels the task as `cancel()` does (cleanups run), throws `task::TimedOut`, and uses the handle up. Both handles. The runtime keeps a timed-out handle's slot until it is taken. A task's own `within:` deadline that ran out makes a later `join` throw `task::TimedOut` again.
4. **`par_iter` with pausing lambdas**: one task per element under admission and `limit:`, polled by the call; results in input order; every failure kept (first in input order thrown, the rest `secondary`), a failure slot only where the lambda can throw, allocated on the failure path; `limit:` replaces `workers:` on `fold`/`par_fold`; `within:`, `admission:` on `par_iter`.
5. `task::Admission`, `task::Load`, `task::Decision` (shape of ADR-326 D2's `net::Admission`); `std`'s default strategy; a task starts only where a descriptor is free (and, after #490, where its block fits); otherwise waits. The descriptor ceiling: at it a task waits, never fails. (Part II's `Admission` block is refused by `rustc` today because `task::Load` does not exist; recorded in `tests/specification/COMPILES.txt`.)
6. After #490: a block per task (ADR-327 D5); a full block unwinds at the allocation, cleanups run, no panic hook, arrives as `task::OverBudget` and runs the fallback; in a group it fails only its task; a `par_iter` lambda that never pauses shares its piece's block, reset per element only where it allocates and keeps memory (async-2 D6).
7. `task::OverBudget` in the C error codes (`1102`).
8. Tests in `tests/language/src/` (`.nika` only): a child handle cancelled while sleeping returns at once and the group still ends; a deferred handle runs only after `start()`; a `join(within:)` that times out, then a second `join()` that gets the value; `on_timeout: task::OnTimeout::Cancel` stops the task (its cleanup runs); admission with a tiny descriptor ceiling waits instead of failing; a pausing `par_iter().map` keeps input order and every failure; after #490, a task over its budget fails with `task::OverBudget` and its sibling completes.

`task::cancel` is **not** built (removed by ADR-async-4 D10). The names are final (async-4 D13).

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/988).

`blocked` · opened 2026-10-30 · updated 2026-10-30 · 0 comments

Part of #983. Records: [ADR-async-4](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-4.md) D2, D4-D8, D10, D14; [ADR-async-2](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-2.md) D2, D5, D6; [ADR-async-3](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-3.md) D7; ADR-async-1 D9, D11, D12, D14. Spec: Part I 8.1.2, 8.2; Part II 12.6, 12.7; Part III `--overlaps`. Needs #986 (checker) and #987 (std/runtime).

## To build
1. Lower `async e`: start the task where it is written (left to right); join it at the wait point the checker placed (before the statement, the call or the operation); hold its outcome until then. The callee receives a plain `T`.
2. A pausing task is polled by its group's future (ADR-328 D10; `emit_core_args.nika` scope code is the starting point); a non-pausing one runs on the pool at `yes`, and at `no` when the main line next pauses or waits (ADR-292 D6 start order).
3. Groups: `async { }` and the innermost block join every unjoined task (child handles included, a handle left live by a timed-out `join(within:)` too) at their end, in written order, before an early exit continues.
4. Handle forms: `async(handle)` → `ChildHandle`; `async(deferred)` starts at `start()`; `async(detached)` → the existing `spawn` lowering (`TaskHandle`); `h.cancel()`; `h.join(within: d)` and `h.join(within: d, on_timeout: task::OnTimeout::Cancel)` (async-4 D14).
5. `limit:` (a counting gate per form, nested gates all held), `within:` — **a deadline counted from the form's start, on every form, value or handle** (async-3 D7): cancel the form's running tasks, `task::TimedOut` where the value is first needed, at the join, or at the group's end — and `admission:`.
6. `par_iter`: pieces for a computing chain, one task per element for a pausing one (the ledger's verdict), with the cost rule of async-2 D6 (no failure slot for a lambda that cannot throw, no block reset for one that does not keep memory).
7. `async xs.par_iter() … .collect()` as one task.
8. Chaining: a task that names a pending binding joins it inside its own body; in a diamond the first mention in written order receives a failure, the other waiters are cancelled.
9. A panic cancels the siblings and the group throws `task::Crashed`; `task::OverBudget` fails only its task.
10. `--overlaps` prints each task, its window, wait point and group, and per `par_iter` call the execution chosen and the call that made a lambda pause.
11. **Measurements owed** (ADR-async-2 D6; callgrind counts only, release on both sides, LTO stated, the same output first; table in `benches/`): `par_iter().map(…).collect()` over 10^6 elements against Rayon, (a) with a lambda that can throw, (b) with a lambda that allocates. The lowering of step 6 is accepted only with these rows.
12. Tests in `tests/language/src/async_*.nika` (both `user_parallelism` settings): a value waited for at first use; `f(async g(), async h())`; `async a() + async b()`; a group waits on early `return`; `limit: 2` never more than two in flight; `async(within:)` throws `task::TimedOut` counted from the start (also on a handle form, at the join); `join(within:)` times out and the task finishes afterwards; chaining; a panic cancels siblings; a pausing `par_iter` keeps order.

# Issue #989: async (ADR-async-4): errors - failure order, started/arrived sites, trace stitching

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/989).

`blocked` · opened 2026-10-30 · updated 2026-10-30 · 0 comments

Part of #983. Records: [ADR-async-4](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-async-4.md) D11; ADR-async-1 D9, D16 (changed), D17. Spec: Part I 7.1 (started and arrived sites), 8.1.2 (*A failure is held until it arrives*), 8.2. Needs #988 (lowering).

## To build
1. **The order, for every form**: a `catch` in the task runs in the task, at once; otherwise the failure is held to where it arrives - the mention that waits (value form) or `h.join()` / `t.join()` (handles) - and an enclosing `catch` there takes it; otherwise the fallback (`catch` directly after the `async` expression) runs: at the wait point for the value form, inside the join for a handle, and **in the task itself when it fails for a detached handle never joined**; otherwise the receiver (the wait point or join throws; unread, the group's end; a detached task nobody joins, standard error).
2. A cancellation is not a failure: no fallback runs. `task::OverBudget` runs it.
3. Unread failures at the group's end (child handles never joined included): the fallback runs for them; on a normal end the first in written order is thrown with the rest as `secondary`; where a failure leaves the group, it leads and the unread ones are its `secondary`, in written order.
4. The `throws` walk: what the fallback throws, or the task's whole set where there is none.
5. `started` and `arrived` sites for every form (the arrived site of a handle is its `join`): compile-time text, one pair per crossing, each `secondary` with its own; nothing on the success path.
6. The long form prints `raised`, `started`, `arrived`; `NIKAIA_TRACE=1` stitches with `── started at <site> ──` per crossing.
7. Tests in `tests/compiler/tests/async_fail_*.nika` with `.stdout`/`.stderr`: each level for the value form and for a handle; a catch at the join beating the fallback; a detached task's fallback running in the task; a cancelled handle running no fallback; unread failures as `secondary`; leaving `throw` leads; the long form's three lines; a chain of two crossings; a `NIKAIA_TRACE=1` run.

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/993).

Part I 8.1.2 (and ADR-292 D3) says two branches that meet on a resource, one of them writing it, are refused with `NK2104`, and names `file(path)` as such a resource. With `target/fast/nikaia` on develop (0.0.1306), this program is accepted:

fn main() throws {
    overlap {
        fs::write("log.txt", fs::Root::Anywhere, "a")

    }
}
